es: Reconocer cómo las palabras y la estructura de un titular encuadran un mismo hecho: enfoque neutral, crítico o positivo.

vocabulary.es: emotivo, que apela a las emociones

teaching.en: A neutral headline only reports what happened: the council raises the bus fare by ten per cent from January.
teaching.es: Un titular neutral solo cuenta lo que pasó: el ayuntamiento sube el precio del autobús un diez por ciento desde enero.
teaching.explanationEs: Raises es un verbo plano: da el hecho sin valoración.
segments: A neutral headline only reports what happened: the council raises
the bus fare by ten per cent from January.
teaching.audioText: A neutral headline only reports what happened: the council raises the bus fare by ten per cent from January.

teaching.en: A loaded headline uses emotive language to steer the reader: residents slam the council over a fare rise that hits every commuter.
teaching.es: Un titular cargado usa un lenguaje emotivo para guiar al lector: los vecinos arremeten contra el ayuntamiento por una subida que golpea a todo viajero diario.
teaching.explanationEs: Slam es un verbo de crítica dura; hits y emotive language cargan la noticia de emoción.
segments: A loaded headline uses emotive language to steer the reader: residents
slam the council over a fare rise that hits every commuter.
teaching.audioText: A loaded headline uses emotive language to steer the reader: residents slam the council over a fare rise that hits every commuter.

teaching.en: Another newspaper may hail the same decision as a boost for the town, which gives the story a completely different angle.
teaching.es: Otro periódico puede aclamar la misma decisión como un impulso para la ciudad, lo que da a la noticia un enfoque completamente distinto.
teaching.explanationEs: Hail y boost son palabras de elogio; el mismo hecho, con ellas, resulta positivo.
segments: Another newspaper may hail the same decision as a boost for
the town, which gives the story a completely different angle.
teaching.audioText: Another newspaper may hail the same decision as a boost for the town, which gives the story a completely different angle.

teaching.en: Every editor has to frame the event somehow, so the choice of a single verb can decide who looks responsible.
teaching.es: Todo editor tiene que encuadrar el hecho de alguna manera, así que la elección de un solo verbo puede decidir quién parece responsable.
teaching.explanationEs: Frame = presentar un hecho desde una perspectiva; no existe una versión sin ningún encuadre.
segments: Every editor has to frame the event somehow, so the
choice of a single verb can decide who looks responsible.
teaching.audioText: Every editor has to frame the event somehow, so the choice of a single verb can decide who looks responsible.

teaching.en: When a decision provokes a backlash, a headline about public anger can hide the fact that the fare rise was small.
teaching.es: Cuando una decisión provoca una reacción adversa, un titular sobre el enfado público puede ocultar que la subida fue pequeña.
teaching.explanationEs: Backlash = reacción adversa del público; destacarla desplaza el foco del hecho a la emoción.
segments: When a decision provokes a backlash, a headline about public anger
can hide the fact that the fare rise was small.
teaching.audioText: When a decision provokes a backlash, a headline about public anger can hide the fact that the fare rise was small.

teaching.en: To spot the angle, underline the verb, ask who is presented as the victim, and compare the headline with a neutral version of the news.
teaching.es: Para detectar el enfoque, subraya el verbo, pregúntate quién aparece como víctima y compara el titular con una versión neutral de la noticia.
teaching.explanationEs: Angle = enfoque; para reconocerlo, compara con la versión neutral y fíjate en la víctima y el responsable.
segments: To spot the angle, underline the verb, ask who is presented as the
victim, and compare the headline with a neutral version of the news.
teaching.audioText: To spot the angle, underline the verb, ask who is presented as the victim, and compare the headline with a neutral version of the news.

prompt.es: Elige el titular neutral entre los tres que cuentan la misma decisión.

choices.text: Commuters slam council after fare rise hits every household
Council raises bus fare by ten per cent from January
Council hails new fare as a boost for local buses

feedback.es: Solo cuenta quién hace qué y cuándo: no hay verbos de crítica ni de elogio, que sí aparecen en los otros titulares.

hint.es: Busca el titular sin verbos cargados de crítica ni de elogio.

origin.text: Three newspapers cover the same council decision, and each one chooses its own headline. Read the options and decide which one simply reports the event.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los vecinos arremeten contra el ayuntamiento: un verbo cargado de enfado.»

feedback.es: Slam significa criticar con dureza y carga la noticia de enfado, a diferencia de un verbo plano como say.

hint.es: Es un verbo de cuatro letras que significa criticar con dureza.

origin.text: The headline says that residents ___ the council, a loaded verb that suggests real anger about the fare rise.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El autor eligió una palabra cargada para darle un enfoque a la noticia.»

answer.text: The writer chose a loaded word to give the story an angle

feedback.es: Una palabra cargada da a la noticia un enfoque: to give the story an angle.

hint.es: Sujeto y verbo primero; al final, el enfoque.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada titular con el enfoque que transmite.

pairs: Council raises the bus fare by ten per cent
Residents slam council over fare rise
Many hail new buses as a boost for commuters
Fare rise sparks backlash from commuters

pairs.es: centrado en la reacción del público

feedback.es: Cada titular elige palabras distintas para el mismo hecho: un verbo plano, un verbo de crítica, palabras de elogio o la reacción adversa.

pairs: Council raises the bus fare by ten per cent
Residents slam council over fare rise
Many hail new buses as a boost for commuters
Fare rise sparks backlash from commuters

pairs.es: centrado en la reacción del público

prompt.es: Escucha el avance informativo y elige el enfoque del segundo periódico.

choices.text: It blames the council for a rise that hurts every commuter.
It reports the rise without adding either praise or blame.
It praises the council for protecting the service.

feedback.es: Presenta la decisión como una forma de proteger el servicio y elogia al ayuntamiento, a diferencia del periódico crítico y del que solo informa.

origin.audio: Good morning. Our top story: the council has raised bus fares. One newspaper says that commuters are hit by the rise. Another says that the council has acted to protect the service. A third simply says that the fare will go up by ten per cent from January. Same decision, three different angles.

prompt.es: ¿Qué diferencia de enfoque hay entre estos dos titulares?

choices.text: The second shows the council ignoring the public; the first only reports.
The second is more accurate because it gives extra detail about how the vote went.
The first blames the public for the decision, while the second stays completely neutral about it.

feedback.es: «Goes ahead … despite public anger» presenta al ayuntamiento como sordo a la protesta; el primer titular se limita al resultado.

origin.text: First headline: Fares up ten per cent after council vote. Second headline: Council goes ahead with ten per cent fare rise despite public anger.

prompt.es: Lee la noticia. ¿Qué efecto tiene la última frase sobre el enfoque del texto?

choices.text: It stays neutral because it only repeats what officials said first.
It highlights the harm to low-paid commuters through critics' words.
It blames the night buses for causing the rise in the fare.

feedback.es: La noticia cierra con la advertencia de los críticos y con «hit hardest»: el lector termina pensando en quienes salen más perjudicados.

origin.text: Town hall confirms that bus fares will rise by ten per cent in January. Officials say that the money will keep night buses running, but critics warn that thousands of low-paid commuters will be hit hardest.

prompt.es: Escucha a la crítica de medios y elige qué pretende al comparar las portadas.

choices.text: To complain about the new tram line and its cost to shops.
To prove that one newspaper is lying about the official figures.
To show that verbs can change how facts look.

feedback.es: Señala que ambos periódicos usan las mismas cifras y cambian solo los verbos: demuestra que el enfoque depende de la elección de palabras.

origin.audio: On the morning show, a media critic compares two front pages about the new tram line. One hails it as a boost for the whole city, while the other says the project has sparked a backlash among shop owners. She points out that both papers use the same figures, but choose different verbs, and those verbs tell the reader how to feel. Her advice is simple: before you share a headline, ask which word is trying to persuade you.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué pregunta aconseja hacerse antes de compartir un titular.

choices.text: Which word is trying to persuade the reader.
Which newspaper published the headline before the others.
Which figures the headline has left out of the story.

feedback.es: Su consejo final es preguntarse qué palabra intenta persuadir: fijarse en el vocabulario cargado, no en el orden de publicación.

origin.audio: On the morning show, a media critic compares two front pages about the new tram line. One hails it as a boost for the whole city, while the other says the project has sparked a backlash among shop owners. She points out that both papers use the same figures, but choose different verbs, and those verbs tell the reader how to feel. Her advice is simple: before you share a headline, ask which word is trying to persuade you.

prompt.es: Completa: «Llamarla «un desastre» es lenguaje cargado: añade un juicio.»

feedback.es: Loaded describe el lenguaje que añade valoración al hecho, como «disaster».

origin.text: A headline that calls a fare rise a disaster for commuters uses ___ language, because it adds a judgement to the fact.

prompt.es: Lee la nota de la editora. ¿Qué reconoce en ella?

choices.text: That the original headline contained a false figure about the new fare.
That the verb made the reaction look stronger than it was.
That the council asked the paper to soften the story afterwards.

feedback.es: Solo dos de cuarenta personas fueron críticas: el verbo slam exageraba la reacción y por eso la editora corrige el titular.

origin.text: Editor's note: Our headline said that residents slam the council, but only two of the forty people we interviewed used negative words. We have changed the headline and we apologise for the idea it gave readers.

prompt.es: Reescribe el titular de forma neutral con los hechos que se dan.

answer.text: Council raises bus fare by ten per cent
accepted: Council raises bus fare by ten per cent
Council raises the fare by ten per cent
Bus fare rises by ten per cent after council decision

feedback.es: Un titular neutral conserva el hecho (quién sube qué y cuánto) y elimina la emoción y los adjetivos cargados.

origin.text: Headline: Angry residents slam council over shock fare rise. Facts: the council decided on Tuesday to raise the fare by ten per cent.

prompt.es: Completa: «Algunos periódicos aclaman los nuevos autobuses como un impulso.»

feedback.es: Hail significa aclamar o elogiar y se usa en titulares para presentar una novedad de forma positiva.

origin.text: Some newspapers ___ the new buses as a boost for the town, while others prefer to focus on the higher fare.
